description:
## Why

CA/B Forum-specific lint bundles (`cabf.br.tls`, `cabf.br.smime`, SC-081 enforcement, etc.) get moved out of `pkix-lint` proper and into a sibling crate with the same reference-not-authoritative framing as `pkix-profiles-cabf`.

## What

1. Create new workspace member `pkix-lint-cabf/` (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, README.md).
2. Cargo.toml deps: `pkix-lint` (framework), `x509-cert`, etc.
3. Crate-level rustdoc header:

   > # pkix-lint-cabf
   >
   > **Reference lint bundles for CA/B Forum Baseline Requirements. Not authoritative.**
   >
   > Lint rules in this crate are a snapshot of CA/B Forum BR requirements at the time of the most recent revision. CA/B Forum ballots regularly add, remove, or alter requirements; the bundles here will lag. They are intended as a starting point: fork and adapt to your deployment's current interpretation of the BR text.
   >
   > For the current Baseline Requirements: see https://cabforum.org/.
   >
   > Maintained on a best-effort basis. Production lint policies SHOULD be authored and reviewed against the live BR text by the consuming organization.

4. README.md mirrors the rustdoc header.

5. Move the following from `pkix-lint`:
   - Anything keyed off a CA/B Forum ballot number (SC-081, etc.).
   - `cabf.br.tls` / `cabf.br.smime` lint rule definitions.
   - Any `EvaluationReport::new("cabf.br.tls", ...)` test fixtures and example values that pin to CA/B Forum bundle identifiers (the `rule_bundle_version` field stays generic in `pkix-lint` rustdoc; examples may move).

6. RFC-conformance lints stay in `pkix-lint` (RFC 5280, RFC 6960, RFC 4518 violations).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pkix-lint-cabf` builds cleanly in the workspace.
- [ ] `cargo check --workspace --all-features` clean.
- [ ] Rustdoc header carries the not-authoritative caveat verbatim.
- [ ] All cabf.br.* lints import from this crate, not from `pkix-lint`.
- [ ] Existing tests move with the code and still pass.
- [ ] Cargo.toml workspace member list updated.
- [ ] Crate version 0.1.0 with publication metadata.

## Out of scope

- Refactoring `pkix-lint` itself to strip the moved content — that's PKIX-amgn.5.

## Depends on

PKIX-amgn.1 (stance anchor).
notes:
OSCAL alignment retrofit (2026-05-11, per PKIX-ztmr stance): content of pkix-lint-cabf MUST be authored AS an OSCAL Catalog + Profile pair, not as a bespoke Rust struct collection. Specifically: the cabf lint rules become OSCAL Controls in a Catalog; cabf.br.tls becomes an OSCAL Profile selecting from that Catalog. This bead now depends on PKIX-9vnx.7 (Profile composition mechanism must exist before authoring cabf.br.tls as a Profile). The 'reference, not authoritative' rustdoc header text stays — it's about authoritativeness of the policy snapshot, orthogonal to the OSCAL data shape.
Closed 2026-05-11: stub crate created. Scope reduced to match PKIX-amgn.2 (scope X — empty skeleton only).

- Crate exists at pkix-lint-cabf/ with Cargo.toml + src/lib.rs + README.md.
- Crate-level rustdoc carries the not-authoritative caveat verbatim.
- README.md mirrors the rustdoc header.
- Workspace Cargo.toml updated (members + workspace.dependencies entry at 0.1.0).
- cargo check --workspace --all-features clean.
- cargo publish --dry-run -p pkix-lint-cabf clean.

The original blocking dependency on PKIX-9vnx.7 (Profile composition via OSCAL) is dissolved — that machinery is needed for the substantive content (lint bundles authored as OSCAL Profiles), which lands in PKIX-amgn.5, not in the stub crate creation.

Publication to crates.io is a maintainer action; see top-level summary for cargo publish command.
title: Create pkix-lint-cabf workspace crate (reference, not authoritative)
